Oracle Fusion HCM 26D: what's new

26D is the next Oracle Fusion Cloud quarterly update. Oracle's 26D What's New documents for this area list 263 features: 89 on by default, 42 on by default with potential setup, 128 setup required, 1 opt-in, 3 needing another action, per Oracle's "Action to Enable" column. See all 263 →

Get the 26D checklist now: what switches on by itself, which former opt-ins are now standard, what to test

Inside the free 26D checklist (PDF):

  • The 23 opt-ins Oracle lists as ending with 26D: 9 switch on for everyone, 14 need setup
  • 9 HCM Redwood default switches and other HCM notices for 26D
  • 9 baseline regression checks, plus typical 26D test and production dates by cohort

Then one plain-English email per Oracle quarterly update, linked to Oracle's docs. Free. 4 emails a year plus short opt-in alerts. Unsubscribe anytime. Read issue #1 (26C) → · Privacy

We track 25 HCM changes in 26D, out of 263 features (our count) in Oracle's 26D What's New documents for this area. 25 of them are delivered switched on; 0 need setup or an opt-in before anyone can use them.

Oracle sources: Absence Management 26D What's New · Benefits 26D What's New · Compensation 26D What's New · Human Resources 26D What's New · Learning and Development 26D What's New · Payroll 26D What's New · Recruiting 26D What's New · Talent Management 26D What's New · Time and Labor 26D What's New · Workforce Scheduling 26D What's New

Oracle had not published 26D What's New documents for Work Life when we last checked, so it is not included yet. We check every week and add it once Oracle publishes.

Impact on upgrade is our editorial rating of how much a change affects existing users and testing; Oracle scale is Oracle's own rating. Always confirm details on the linked Oracle page.

Former opt-ins now standard in 26D

From Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list: features whose opt-in period ends with 26D. If you already opted in and finished setup, nothing changes. All former opt-ins now standard in 26D →

None in Oracle's list.

HCM: pages switching to Redwood in 26D (9)

Oracle announces these HCM changes in its HCM What's New documents as Redwood default switches (and a few end-of-support, migration or removal notices), not as opt-in expirations. They are not on Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list and are not part of the former opt-ins counts on this site. All HCM pages switching to Redwood →

Redwood person pages by default (moved from 26C)

Global HRSwitches to Redwood by defaultFrom 26DRevert: Profile option can be set back to No

Six person pages switch to Redwood by default in 26D; Oracle had planned this for 26C.

Pages affected: Personal Details, Contact Info, Identification Info, Family and Emergency Contacts, Additional Person Info, Person Identifiers for External Applications

Profile options named on Oracle's page: ORA_PER_PERSONAL_INFORMATION_REDWOOD_ENABLED, ORA_PER_ADDITIONAL_PERSONAL_INFO_REDWOOD_ENABLED, ORA_PER_PERSON_IDENTIFIERS_FOR_EXT_APP_REDWOOD_ENABLED

Responsive Career Development pages no longer supported

LearningMigrationFrom 26DRevert: None stated: automatic move to Redwood in 27A

Responsive Career Development pages are no longer supported after 26D; anyone still on them moves to Redwood automatically in 27A.

Pages affected: Me > Career > Career Development, My Team > Career Overview > Performance

Oracle's title: “Mandatory migration to Redwood Career Development”

Oracle source

Old recommendations framework stops

LearningRemovalFrom 26DRevert: None stated

If the new Recommendations framework (available since 25A) is not enabled before 26D, recommendations no longer appear in Oracle Learning.

Pages affected: Recommendations in Oracle Learning

Oracle source

Process Automation task type removed from journey setup

JourneysRemovalFrom 26DRevert: None stated

From 26D you can no longer create journey tasks with the Process Automation task type; Oracle Process Automation reaches end of life on 31 October 2026.

Pages affected: Journey templates, task groups and task library

Oracle source

Create Time Card Calculation Component process disabled

PayrollRemovalFrom 26DRevert: None stated

From 26D the Create Time Card Calculation Component process is disabled; Oracle asks you to reimplement upgraded time elements by 27D.

Pages affected: Time elements upgraded with Create Time Card Calculation Component

Oracle source

Digital Assistant on recruiting sites phased out

RecruitingEnd of supportFrom 26DRevert: None stated

From November 2026 Oracle no longer supports Digital Assistant Fusion Apps templates; only sites that already use it keep it for now.

Pages affected: Recruiting career sites using Digital Assistant

Oracle source

Enhanced Statutory Parental Bereavement Leave and Pay for Northern Ireland Employees

Impact on upgrade: highOracle scale: Larger scaleAutomatically onHCMPayroll · Payroll for the United Kingdom
From 6 April 2026, an enhanced statutory parental bereavement pay process applies to employees gainfully employed in Northern Ireland. It extends payment eligibility to miscarriage-related absences and provides day-one eligibility.
Oracle's "Impact to Existing Processes": Larger scale · Action to enable: None · Oracle source

Enhancements for Absence Integration on Redwood Time Cards

Impact on upgrade: highOracle scale: Larger scaleAutomatically onHCMTime and Labor · Time and LaborRedwood Platform
Align absence removal with Absence Management processing and give workers and approvers clearer visibility into the related approval flow. When you remove an absence from a Redwood time card, the application deletes or withdraws it based on the absence status and applies the configured approval rules.
Oracle's "Impact to Existing Processes": Larger scale · Action to enable: None · Oracle source

Default Sorting by Name in Absence Planning

Impact on upgrade: mediumOracle scale: Small scaleAutomatically onHCMAbsence Management · Absence Management

All 263 HCM features in Oracle's 26D What's New

Every row of the Feature Summary tables in Oracle's 26D What's New documents for this area, with Oracle's own "Impact to Existing Processes" and "Action to Enable" columns as Oracle states them: 89 on by default, 42 on by default with potential setup, 128 setup required, 1 opt-in, 3 needing another action. Oracle's legend: features whose impact is "None" are not delivered enabled and need steps to use; "Potential Setup" means there is prerequisite or optional configuration to consider. Each title links to Oracle's feature page.
